crime: For several evenings, a girl practiced pool alone in the recreation room while {WITCH_NAME} reracked the balls and recorded every shot without error. Each night, the player promised that {WITCH_NAME} could play the next game. Before the last rack one evening, she made the promise again.

When that rack ended, another girl arrived. The player gave her the promised game, began a new rack with her, and asked {WITCH_NAME} to keep score again. The newcomer committed an obvious foul on her first turn. The player laughed and let her continue. The newcomer later went alone to the lounge to wait for dinner, and {WITCH_NAME} left the recreation room separately.

Before dinner, the player entered the lounge and found the newcomer dead on the floor beside a sofa. A narrow thrust through the side of her neck had severed her airway and a major blood vessel. The wound had two close punctures beside two short cuts. Their spacing matched the forked tip and two shallow notches of one old sword on the lounge rack.

Yet that sword was still in place. A brittle layer of dry corrosion remained unbroken across its tip and notches, with no scrapes and no blood, so the original had not made the fresh wound. No other prison blade had the same fork width and notch spacing.

{WITCH_NAME} had entered while the newcomer sat with her back turned. She touched only the distinctive sword's hilt, made an exact copy appear in her hand without moving the original, and drove the copy through the newcomer's neck. She kept hold until the girl stopped breathing, then released it and let the weapon vanish. Only a copy could explain the matching wound and untouched original, and because the copy remained solid only against {WITCH_NAME}'s skin, {WITCH_NAME} had held the killing weapon.
fields.epitaph: At last, every edge matched—and nothing inside still answered to her name.
execution: An upright iron body mold stands open around her in two thick halves. They close over her head, arms, torso, and legs, drawing every limb into one exact outline. Once the mold presses against her whole body, it keeps pressing inward and leaves her no room to shift. It crushes her ribs, throat, and skull until she stops breathing and moving and dies.

magic.name: Copying Hand
magic.text: She can make an exact copy of an object.
